chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the divorce of the intoxicated one, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not valid, and there is no prestige (or: it is not a matter of grace/discretion).'

key_terms.لَا كَرَامَة: No prestige / Not a matter of grace

ai.seo_question: Is a divorce valid if pronounced by an intoxicated person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the divorce of an intoxicated person is not valid, a ruling derived from the principle that intoxication removes the faculty of reason (aql) necessary for legal accountability. The phrase 'wa la karamah' is interpreted by Shia jurists to mean that the divorce is not binding even as an act of grace or concession, distinguishing it from cases where intent might be presumed despite minor distractions. This hadith is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the validity of talaq based on the preservation of mental clarity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al Halby who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a divorce by the intoxicated one, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Not allowed, and there is no prestige’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sinan from ibn Muskan from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “
I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the divorce of a drunken man. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not permissible and it is not an honorable thing.’”
